£30,000 Salary After Tax UK

On a £30,000 salary in England, Wales or Northern Ireland you take home £25,120 a year in 2026/27: £2,093 a month, £483 a week or £12.88 an hour on a 37.5-hour week. You pay £3,486 Income Tax and £1,394 National Insurance, so you keep 83.7% of your gross pay.

Where £30,000 sits in the UK tax system

Comfortably basic rate

Every pound between £12,570 and £50,270 is taxed at 20% plus 8% NI, so you keep 72p of each extra pound (28% in deductions). You are £20,270 below the higher-rate threshold.

Student loans bite early

Your loan payment depends heavily on the plan. On £30,000: Plan 1 £279 a year, Plan 2 £55, Plan 5 £450, and a postgraduate loan £540.

Pension costs less than it looks

A 5% pension is £1,500 a year, but take-home falls by only £1,200 through net pay, or £1,080 through salary sacrifice, thanks to tax and NI relief.

What would a pay change do to your take-home?

Compare your salary above with a raise, promotion or job offer. Higher-rate tax, National Insurance and student loan all change how much you keep.

+£10,000 gross+£600 / month net

Moving from £30,000 to £40,000 changes your take-home by +£7,200 a year (+£600 a month). You keep 72% of the extra gross pay; the rest goes in Income Tax and National Insurance. Your next pound at the new salary is taxed at a combined 28%.

Frequently asked questions

How much is £30,000 a year after tax in the UK?

In 2026/27, £30,000 leaves £25,120 a year after £3,486 Income Tax and £1,394 National Insurance in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. That is £2,093 a month.

How much is £30,000 a month after tax?

About £2,093 a month, or £483 a week, assuming tax code 1257L and no pension or student loan.

What is the hourly rate for £30,000?

Before tax, £30,000 is £15.38 an hour on a 37.5-hour week (£14.42 on 40 hours). After tax it is £12.88 an hour.

What tax band is £30,000 in?

The basic-rate band. You pay 20% on pay over £12,570, and your marginal rate including 8% NI is 28%.

How much less would I take home in Scotland on £30,000?

Scottish taxpayers on £30,000 pay £35 less Income Tax in 2026/27 than in the rest of the UK.

Does a student loan change £30,000 after tax?

Yes. A Plan 2 loan would take £55 a year on this salary, leaving £25,064. Use the calculator above to try your own plan.
